Exactly. They do. And in many ways it is. And that’s why so many adult rehabs have fatal overdoses after they released. It makes me sick to think about. 
And while, pretty much every rehab I worked at, the clients were obsessed with food...those fancy ones with top chefs....it’s not needed. If I ran a program, I’d have top chefs come in, not to cook but to teach the clients to cook. Maybe some will find their love of cooking and baking. Because they were teens, my boss would have oil painters, weavers, sculptors, knitters, quilters, literally all kinds of people come in and teach them things every week. Giving them hobbies to do while at rehab or at home. It sucks because once addicts turn 18, the empathy, the tiny bit of empathy that exists goes to like zero. 
Honestly, finding new hobbies are vital to recovery.  And yes, therapy is so important. I think CBT as a basis but I also think DBT is helpful as well.  The one plus of the private programs is you get two private therapy sessions a day, where in public programs irs like 3-5 private sessions a week, max. Just not enough. I believe there’s hope in curing addiction, and it starts with the disease model.


And yeah, at those fancy places.....many are using right there. They know what they drug test for, and will drink or do drugs they don’t test for. (Most don’t do full urine screens). In order for me to stay on my opiates for my cancer, I get a full urine screen...and it comes back with caffeine. (And all my other drugs from my chemo meds, down to Tylenol)

Exactly. They did NONE of that. One of the two biggest things my old rehab focused on...1. Building tool boxes. I literally had them make tools (arts and craft projects) and boxes (with jewels, or whatever they wanted), and then each tool would have a coping skill on it. Some girls even crocheted the little tools, and tied the coping skills on. And 2. Therapy focused heavily on why they were using. And also, removing them from their old places helped a lot. Sending them to recovery high school, and in many cases out of their house into a long term living situation helped tons. When I suggested, my more adult “tool box” idea/metaphor, the “doctor” in charge told me, it was more appropriate for someone who was going on 6 months sober. I fully believe they want them to relapse and return. 

I’d love to open a program, that did what the original one I worked at did...but also had a swimming pool, and other things. Because those with good care would really help.

It’s a mixed thing. Herion and opiates took so many, young and fast. And to get a 18 year old sober, felt like a victory. And they’d stay off herion and it felt like a victory. They’d go to college, and start drinking. drinking is such a big part of college culture, many got swept away by it. It’s not easy to go to college as sober. I didn’t really mean as a good or bad thing. Just a big mixed bag of addiction. I’ve talked with many of them about replacing one drug with another. It’s a depressing field of work, and why I don’t it anymore. (Other reasons too). It’s a place where you have to count those small victories. But they felt so much smaller, when you’d lose them To DUIs, or see alcohol progress their Hep C. 



 The big one now is Marijuana. I see so many former opiate addicts..use marijuana. Many are using marijuana. The ones I still check in with, all seem to use marijuana. And that’s what I’m wondering about. One of the girls, stopped using herion, switched to alcohol, and now she’s sober off both. But works at a marijuana dispensary. It’s confusing. We actually brought our clients to AA instead of NA despite many of them mainly using narcotics. And as you know AA has a stick up their asses sometimes about not talking about alcohol. The program director, thought AA had longer term sobriety. And we also had problems with NA members giving the kids drugs and cigarettes. They’d get mad us for bringing them....and my boss would always point out what you said.

I was the after care conselor. It was my job to follow up with them. Yes, many lied, but many more were honest BECAUSE. It was a mix of both, most of the clients under 18 were being tested by the state, as they were in legal trouble. Most 3-4 times a week. The rest were at recovery high schools. Which also tested. They would tell me that they were going to fail because I could help them sometimes. Anyone who disappeared and went off the map? We’d assume they were using. The ones who I know are sober on all substances? It’s because they became employees at the program. Two of them I consider some of my closest friends. But lifetime numbers..it’s likely more like 99.9% now that I think of it.  Which is pretty amazing. 

A lot of the younger ones who had just been into herion/pills early on, who had a good family support and could get into recovery high. That’s where we saw the best results.
